data.claim: shutil.copytree(s, s/sub, dirs_exist_ok=True) returns (no exception) and copies one level deep into the subtree; FakeFs.copy_tree raises ValueError there, so the fake diverges from LocalFs.
data.falsifier: shutil.copytree(s, s/sub, dirs_exist_ok=True) raises Error/ValueError (it does not)
data.mechanism: shutil.copytree snapshots os.scandir(src) entries before os.makedirs(dst, exist_ok=True) and iterates the snapshot, so a dst inside src terminates after one level
data.probe: scratch python3 shutil.copytree(s, s/sub, dirs_exist_ok=True) on a nested tree {s/top.txt, s/sub/deep/d.txt, s/sub/n.txt}
data.probe_output: RETURNED OK; tree gains s/sub/top.txt and s/sub/sub/{deep/d.txt,n.txt}. move(file,file)/move(dir,dir) no-op OK. copytree(s,s,dirs_exist_ok=True)=shutil.Error; copytree(s,s/sub) dirs_exist_ok=False=FileExistsError.
data.question: Does FakeFs.copy_tree diverge from shutil.copytree / LocalFs on copy-into-own-subtree with dirs_exist_ok=True, and must the fake raise ValueError there?

evidence.note: Empirically probed shutil 3.14.7: copytree(s,s/sub,dirs_exist_ok=True) returns (one level deep); move(file,file)/move(dir,dir) no-op; copytree(s,s)=shutil.Error. Recorded R0bb17d1207 CONFIRMED.
